findings.title: Online channel is elevated in Development
findings.evidence: 0.943% fraud rate; 6.68x lift; 64.3% of fraud transactions.
findings.meaning: Channel is both risk-elevated and material enough to warrant deeper behavioral analysis.
findings.next_action: Test channel-specific velocity and amount-deviation questions in Part 4 using strict prior history.

findings.title: Risk is not the same as exposure
findings.evidence: Development contains 9,673,486 transactions and 13,661 fraud-labeled transactions; signed fraud amount share is 0.351%.
findings.meaning: Prevalence, fraud count and signed amount must be read together before prioritizing a segment.
findings.next_action: Carry both count-based and amount-based views into later decision economics.

findings.title: 250–500 is the highest-lift amount band
findings.meaning: The band is a descriptive hypothesis, not a production rule or loss estimate.
findings.next_action: Test amount-context and card-history behavior in Part 4; do not finalize a threshold here.

findings.title: Entity concentration is visible at the merchant_identifier level
findings.evidence: The top 1% of merchant_identifier entities account for 92.7% of fraud transactions; 439 entities have repeated fraud labels.
findings.meaning: Retrospective concentration motivates history features while remaining distinct from a point-in-time model feature.
findings.next_action: Reconstruct prior entity history in Part 4 with timestamps strictly less than T0.
